name: Red Bay Basque Whaling Station
description: At Red Bay, on Labrador's coast along the Strait of Belle Isle, Basque sailors set up a summer whaling base in the 1530s. They hunted whales from the shore and boiled the blubber into oil that lit lamps across Europe. Today you can see the remains of rendering ovens, wharves, a cemetery and whale bones, and divers can explore sunken ships. The station was abandoned after about 70 years, once the whales were depleted.
